To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the folding pathway of an amphipatic peptide at an interface is dominated by amphipathic structures and that the folding timescale of the peptide is increased by the energetic and entropic cost associated with the successive amphipathicity changes.
amphipathic peptides are strongly adsorbed to a hydrophobic/hydrophilic interface, and that their folding proceeds through a pathway involving successive amphipathics.

(i) the folding of the amphipathic LQQLL QQLLQ sequence proceeds through a pathway characterized by successive amphipathicity; and (ii) the formation of type I turns is an important event during the folding process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the folding of the capped peptide LQQLLQLLQL, a peptide with a sequence that is amphipathic and hydrophobic.
the folding of the capped LQLQL peptide in the water–hexa- ne interface.
the folding of a peptide at an aqueous–organic interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amphipathic structure is the most favorable conformation at the hexane–water interface, but the formation of a helix, which is the most favorable in bulk water, is strongly disfavored.
the folding of the amphipathic sequence LQQLL QQLLQL is strongly facilitated at an oil‐water interface.
the folding of LQQLQQLLQL at the water–hydrocarbon interface proceeds through a pathway involving a succession of amphipathic conformations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the folding of an α‐helix is a very difficult task.
the folding of the peptide at the interface is a slow process.

the amphipathic nature of the sequence, the hydrophobicity of the interface, and the presence of a type I turn at one of its ends are the major factors determining the folding pathway of the LQQLLQLLQL peptide at the interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
folding in interfacial environments proceeds via a different pathway than that of the same sequence in aqueous solutions.
the folding pathway of LQQL‐LQQL‐LQL at the water–hydrocarbon interface involves successive amphipathical intermediates.

the folding pathway of the amphipathic LQQLLQLLQQL peptide is strongly biased by the interfacial environment, which is characterized by the presence of two water phases separated by the hydrophobic hexane.
